chunks: What Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from a group of our companions, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him):
He said: The deceased should not be shrouded in linen.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased; the dead person who is to be washed (ghusl), shrouded (takfin), and buried
key_terms.كَتَّانٍ: linen; cloth woven from flax (Linum usitatissimum), the use of which for the funeral shroud is prohibited

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use linen (kattan) as a funeral shroud in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a concise legal ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibiting the use of linen (kattan — cloth woven from flax fibres) for the funeral shroud (kafan). It forms the jurisprudential basis for the Shia position, enshrined in this very chapter of al-Istibsar, that the kafan must be exclusively of cotton (qutn); linen, silk, and other materials are not permitted.
